purpose: Two declared-output IRQ targets in one real host OR group must be jointly active at the single native CPU take, which the shared observer refuses as ambiguous with zero credit.
case_note: ZipTimer o_int (Wishbone) and PULP SPI events_o (APB3) are the two real members of one OR group. The fixed case program clears mstatus.MIE, writes COUNT(0x0)=8 and INTCFG(0x24)=0x80000000 in that order (real CPU stores, the same working values as declared-irq-f5-wb-timer and declared-irq-f5-apb-spi), sets mstatus.MIE and parks. The timer counts down from 8 and pulses ~6 CPU ticks after its write; the SPI event pulses ~1 tick after its write, so both host pulses are high at the enable. The observed member is the timer: the fixed ISR reads COUNT(0x0), which has no side effect, so the read cannot re-fire the SPI event (the SPI INTSTA read re-arms and re-pulses, which is why the SPI observed case keeps the proven F5 width). pulse_width_ticks=22 leaves ~13 ticks between the enable and the first pulse's end (measured per-word spacing of the fixed program) and still expires well before the real MRET (the F5 handler returns 46-47 CPU ticks after the take).
